title: Quarterly orchestration lanebook: aligning sprint lanes, capacity buffers, and canary windows for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Khan
project: Hosted API + Model Catalog Quarterly Runway
description:
Purpose: Produce an operational 'lanebook' that transforms high-level quarterly commitments into concrete sprint lanes, capacity hedges, and canary windows for the Hosted API and Model Catalog initiatives. This ticket captures the cross-functional plan (PM, Eng, Design, SRE) for Q2 readiness and acts as the single source of truth for execution decisions and trade-offs.

Scope:
- Define 3 rollout lanes (Canary, Ramp, General Availability) with explicit guardrails and rollback criteria.
- Determine per-lane capacity reservations and burst policies for Dedicated vs Hosted tiers.
- Establish canary windows and metrics (latency p95, error-rate, token cost delta, model quality regressions) required to promote between lanes.
- Create a sprint-by-sprint mapping of initiatives to lanes, owners, and required engineering tickets.
- Produce a simple ops runbook for post-deploy regression triage tied to the Console dashboards and alerts.

Goals / success metrics:
- All new Hosted API model additions have a documented lane and canary plan before staging (completion target: 2026-04-03).
- 95% of canaries measure and report against agreed metrics automatically in Console.
- Capacity hedges defined such that 99% of projected burst use can be accommodated without customer-facing throttling.

Deliverables:
- Lanebook doc (Confluence): lane definitions, metric thresholds, promotion checklist. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/quarterly-lanebook-q2 (draft).
- Sprint mapping spreadsheet: per-sprint owner, estimate, dependency, PRDs referenced. Link: Drive > /Team/PM/HostedAPI_Q2_lanebook.xlsx
- Ops runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/214

Key stakeholders: PM leads (Aisha Khan, Marco Chen), Eng leads (Priya Patel, Tomas Rivera), SRE (Liam O'Connor), Design (Sofia Martinez), Solutions Eng (Jordan Lee).

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Conservative canary windows increase time-to-GA but reduce risk; balancing with business need for throughput of new models.
- Dedicated capacity reservations increase cost but reduce customer-impact risk; propose tiered hedges (10% baseline + 25% burst for top-tier customers).
- Automated metric collection requires two Console integrations; one is in flight (ENG-41207) and may delay full automation—temporary manual checks documented in runbook.

Risks:
- Upstream runtime kernel upgrades (runtime-1.21 -> runtime-1.22) could alter p95 latency baselines during canaries. Contingency: freeze kernel changes within canary windows or run side-by-side A/B kernels for critical endpoints.
- Supply-side GPU constraints in early Q2 could block Dedicated hedges; mitigation: convertible burst credits and staged promotions to GA.

Next steps / immediate asks:
1) Engineering to confirm estimated ticket breakouts and identify any blocking infra work (ASSIGNEE: Priya Patel) — due 2026-03-18.
2) SRE to propose alert thresholds and escalation contacts for canary failures (ASSIGNEE: Liam O'Connor) — due 2026-03-20.
3) PM to finalize lane thresholds and publish lanebook draft for review (ASSIGNEE: Marco Chen) — due 2026-03-22.

Notes: This lanebook is intentionally prescriptive to reduce real-time judgement during launches. We will review outcomes at the Q2 retrospective and iterate lane thresholds based on observed regressions and cost impact.
